doc.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: Journalists as historians of the moment
summary: Journalists report jazz as it happens, like reporting from the front lines.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: know I think I got a little off there. But there are things that jazz journalists do for the art form. We are the historians. We are writing the history in the moment that it’s happening. We’re not waiting until everybody’s dead and then trying to go back and do the research. We’re out there on the front lines, seeing concerts, at the clubs, getting the records and we’re telling you what’s happening now. We may not be benefiting from having a historical perspective but I think that we’re benefiting from being there as it’s going down. And this is music that takes place in the moment and I think it deserves to have reportage from the moment. You don’t report a war six years later. You report it from the front lines. And this is not a war, this is a cultural creation and it’s exciting to be there while it’s being created and bringing back these nuggets about what happened, how it happened, who did it, what they were thinking. It’s the same five — who, what, when, where and why thing — and we can apply it to the creation of an art. It’s very exciting.
